problem: End-to-end RL-trained navigation agents are mostly studied in simulation with teleport-style motion and high-level semantics; it is unknown what they actually learn (dynamics, memory, planning) when deployed as fast-moving real robots.
motivation: Bono et al. showed that training with a realistic dynamical motion model in simulation greatly improves sim2real transfer for fast navigation. The paper asks what internal reasoning emerges from such training, and tests it with large-scale real-robot experiments plus probing and sensitivity analyses.
key_idea: Analyze a PPO-trained recurrent PointGoal agent with a realistic motion model, using sensitivity analysis, hidden-state probing, memory ablation, value-function inspection and expert-planner comparison, to show it learns Kalman-like prediction/correction, short-horizon plans and scene memory.
insight: Sensitivity analysis shows the agent relies most on odometry (correction) while also depending on learned dynamics; the agent trained without dynamics overfits to teleportation and collapses when dynamics change (SR 27.6 vs 97.6 in sim+dyn). Linear probes of the hidden state predict future pose (0.44m position error over ~6s with a prev-action input), so latent dynamics and short plans exist, but no evidence of correct long-term plans ('tunnel vision'). Memory ablation (zeroing h every 3s drops SR 100→75) and value-estimate jumps at re-planning suggest memory holds exploration info.
method: Base agent: PointGoal policy with ResNet-18 RGB, 1D-CNN scan, odometry, AMCL localization and prev-action encoders feeding a 2-layer GRU (1024 hidden), linear policy over 28 discrete velocity pairs, trained with PPO for 500M steps; auxiliary head predicts relative goal.
Realistic motion model: second-order dynamical model (response time, damping, max velocity) identified from the real robot and placed between policy (3Hz) and Habitat (integration at 30Hz).

Input-vs-model sensitivity with 'distance to belief': perturb dynamics parameters or odometry noise, and normalize the perturbations by the average trajectory divergence (meters) over 1,000 action sequences, to compare SR drops.
RMA-style adaptation: train with randomized dynamics parameters and feed an environment embedding to the policy to show the drop from dynamics shift can be recovered.
Probing: linear probes from h_t to future poses (20 steps), a local 3x3m occupancy map, and a rollout with the agent's own GRU; Shapley values for input modalities.

Real-world ablations and planning analysis: memory zeroing, speed clipping, decision delay, visual localization replacement, PPO value curves, and a Fast Marching Square expert cost giving a planning-quality heatmap.

setting.backbone: ResNet-18 + 1D-CNN + 2-layer GRU recurrent PPO policy (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: HM3D train scenes in Habitat with the identified dynamics model, 500M env steps, PPO RL; no extra data
setting.observation: RGB + 4-depth-sensor lidar-like scan + wheel odometry + AMCL localization + static point goal
setting.action_space: 28 discrete linear/angular velocity command pairs at 3Hz
setting.simulator: Habitat (HM3D) with a dynamical motion model; real Rookie robot in an office building
setting.privileged: none at test time (onboard odometry and AMCL localization used as inputs; the goal is given as coordinates)

numbers.eval_set_note: 2,500 HM3D val episodes with simulated dynamics model
numbers.extra: trained with realistic dynamics model, 500M steps, test-time RGB augmentation; success radius 0.2m

numbers.eval_set_note: real robot, 20 episodes per run, 4 runs (80 episodes), mean of 4 runs
numbers.extra: sim2real on a real Rookie robot; success radius 1m; max speed clipped to 70%; std SR ±2.9, SPL ±5.0, SCT ±3.0

numbers.eval_set_note: 2,500 HM3D val episodes with simulated dynamics model
numbers.method: D28-instant (own baseline variant, no dynamics in training)
numbers.extra: trained without dynamical model, evaluated with dynamics

numbers_note: PointNav in Habitat with a dynamics model, not the standard PointNav benchmark protocol. Ablation numbers on the 14-episode real subset are not listed.
results: The dynamics-trained agent reaches 97.6 SR / 82.3 SPL in simulation with dynamics and 92.5 SR in the real office, far above D28-instant (27.6 SR in sim+dyn, 10.0 real) and D4 (29.1 sim, 0.0 real). Probing, ablation and value analyses show latent dynamics, scene memory and short-horizon plans, but no correct long-term planning.
limitations: Only PointGoal navigation in a single real building (20 episodes per run), so the conclusions are demonstrated for a narrow setting
The evidence for planning is qualitative or post-hoc (a single-episode value curve, heatmaps); the agent shows 'tunnel vision' and no correct long-term plans
Performance gains from engineering changes (500M steps, sin/cos angle inputs, test-time augmentation) were not ablated
builds_on: Bono et al. 2024 (Learning to navigate efficiently and precisely in real environments)
